grades.quote: The manner in which interrupts are generated, routed to, and enabled by a hart depends on the EEI.
grades.reason: General RISC-V definition of interrupts and traps. It only notes that how interrupts are generated, routed and enabled depends on the EEI. It names no specific conditions (global enable, masking, delegation, privilege level) that stop a pending interrupt from reaching its handler.

OS textbook text about thread scheduling and thread states, with a timer interrupt handler as an example. It says nothing about architectural conditions that block a pending interrupt from entering its handler.
xv6 driver concurrency discussion about locks and what interrupt handlers may do. It does not describe any condition that keeps a pending interrupt from being taken.

This is only the figure for the mip (interrupt-pending) register. It shows where pending bits are held but gives no conditions that stop a pending interrupt from being taken (mie, mstatus.MIE, mideleg, privilege level). It is limited auxiliary context.
